messages:
Diego: hey everyone! i'm Diego (backend)  day 2. trying to look at a prod flag in Console to correlate with customer logs but hitting a 403 on the /admin/flags/<flag-name> page. who owns short-lived prod access or the JIT path?

Molly: welcome @Diego :wave: prod flag edits are locked down. do you only need read access or do you actually need to flip it?

Diego: just need to view the state + recent audit entries to trace a mismatch. no toggle needed if possible.

Irene: for read-only, we have the ff-auditors role. if you need to script it, we can either create a scoped service token (requires ticket) or run a JIT that grants read for a short window. which is easier for you?

Diego: scripting would be ideal (want to run a one-off snapshot script), but if the ticket flow is long a JIT is fine. i tried the UI and got this curl failure first:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://console.redwood.ai/admin/flags/customer-ux-experiment
# response: 403 {"error":"forbidden","reason":"insufficient_scope"}
```

Ben: pinging @Irene for sponsor. @Diego file a short Linear ticket with the purpose + expected expiry. include who owns audit review. ops/security prefer service tokens for automated nightly jobs.

admin-bot: Access template: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/access-requests. Category: service-account-readonly or jit-elevation.

Diego: opened ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PROD-6009  purpose: one-time snapshot of prod flags to debug customer mismatch. requested expiry: 2 hours.

Irene: sponsoring now. note: service tokens > long-lived tokens; for a one-off we can schedule a JIT for the CI job to grab a short-lived token. i'll approve and set expiry to 1.5 hours.

admin-bot: JIT request created: JIT-6009 by Irene. Approve here: https://console.redwood.ai/jit/JIT-6009

Ben: FYI if you're automating later, use infra-tools/jit-helper which calls the JIT API and emits a token. It still needs a sponsor approver or an approver service account.

Diego: approved the JIT prompt. thanks! got a token and fetched the audit entries. found that the flag was toggled by a release pipeline 3 days ago. copying audit id: audit-2026-03-22-6009 into the ticket.

Molly: good catch. can you paste the relevant audit line in the ticket and add a 1-sentence next step? security wants rollback windows and owners logged.

Diego: done — added timestamp, audit id, and a short follow-up to add a staging check. reverted nothing (read-only).

Irene: perfect. pro-tip for new hires: if you need to run this regularly, request a scheduled JIT triggered by CI rather than a permanent token. less compliance overhead.

Diego: will do. thanks for the quick help and welcome notes :smile:
